points.why: It frames the question as whether plausible input errors push the reduction below the 10% target, and notes the 8-point margin.
It swings each input across a plausible range with the others at baseline, flags any that can pull the result below 10%, and offers a tornado analysis.
It adds a joint Monte Carlo analysis as a global method but never says one-at-a-time swings miss inputs that matter only together, and names neither Morris nor Sobol.
It aims for a ranking and recommends buying only the top 2–4 inputs instead of the full $400k package.
